units.title: Fashion
units.intro: Grammar: the present continuous for actions continuing over a period, and confusing verbs (accept/except, adapt/adopt).

lessons.title: Present continuous for a period of time

cards.title: Present continuous for a period of time
rule: **am/is/are + -ing** describes actions happening now **or around now**, over a period: *Young people **are wearing** traditional clothes again this year.* It also shows changing trends: *Fashion **is becoming** more expensive.*
State verbs (*know, like, want, belong, understand*) are not normally used in the continuous: *I **like** this dress* (not *am liking*).

examples.text: These days many students are learning to sew.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: I failed the national biology matriculation exam; I ________ harder instead of wasting my time on social media.

steps.text: The context 'I failed...; I [blank] harder' indicates a past regret or criticism of an action that was advisable but did not happen.
This requires the past regret modal structure ($$\text{should have} + \text{V}_3$$).
Students often confuse 'must have studied' (logical deduction of fact) with 'should have studied' (regret).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: According to the laboratory safety rules, you ________ enter the chemistry room without wearing safety goggles.

steps.text: The context describes a strict laboratory safety rule.
This requires a modal of prohibition to show the action is forbidden ($$\text{must not} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).
Students often confuse 'don't have to' (lack of obligation/optional) with 'must not' (prohibition/forbidden).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Aster has been studying and living in London for ten years, so she ________ speak English very fluently.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context presents strong present evidence ('living in London for ten years'). This requires a modal of present logical deduction to show high certainty ($$\text{must} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students sometimes choose 'must have' (Option D), but 'must have' is for past deduction ($$\text{must have} + \text{V}_3$$) and cannot be followed by the base verb 'speak'. Option A is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እቲ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ኣብ ህልው እዋን ዘሎ ናይ ምርግጋጽ ስነ-ሞጎት (present logical deduction) የርእየና። 'ዓሰርተ ዓመት ኣብ ሎንዶን ስለ ዝነበረት' ዝብል መርትዖ ስለ ዘሎ፡ 'ብርግጽ ብጽቡቕ ትዛረብ እያ' ንምባል 'must' (Option A) ክንጥቀም ኣለና። 'must have' ግን ንሕሉፍ እዋን ጥራይ እዩ ዘገልግል።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The soccer field is completely covered in puddles; it ________ heavily during the night.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The present evidence 'The soccer field is completely covered in puddles' leads to a strong positive deduction about a past event. This requires 'must have' ($$\text{must have} + \text{V}_3$$).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'should have rained' (past regret/unrealized advice) with 'must have rained' (past deduction of fact). Option A is incorrect because we are deducing a fact based on physical evidence, making Option B correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'እቲ ናይ ኲዕሶ እግሪ ሜዳ ብማይ ተሸፊኑ ኣሎ' ዝብል ናይ ዓይኒ መርትዖ ስለ ዘለና፡ 'ትማሊ ምሸት ብርግጽ ዓቢ ዝናብ ዘኒቡ ክኸውን ኣለዎ' (past logical deduction) ንምባል 'must have rained' (Option B) ክንመርጽ ኣለና። 'should have' ግን ጣዕሳ ጥራይ እዩ ዝገልጽ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Why are you walking to school?" "My bicycle is broken, so I ____ this week."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** "this week" and the broken bicycle show a temporary situation.

**Step 2:** Use the present continuous: am walking.

**Step 3:** The present simple would suggest a permanent habit.

**Tip:** Present continuous can describe a temporary situation around now (this week, these days). Watch confusing pairs: lie/lay, rise/raise, borrow/lend, wear/dress.

cards.title: Confusing verbs
rule: **accept** = agree to take (*accept a gift*); **except** = not including (preposition: *everyone **except** me*).
**adapt** = change to suit (*adapt to a new climate*); **adopt** = take as your own (*adopt a new style; adopt a child*).

examples.text: He adapted quickly to city life.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "Everyone came accept Ruth."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** **accept** = agree to take (*accept a gift*); **except** = not including (preposition: *everyone **except** me*).
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "Everyone came accept Ruth." breaks this rule.
**Check:** **adapt** = change to suit (*adapt to a new climate*); **adopt** = take as your own (*adopt a new style; adopt a child*).

cards.title: Memory tip
body: acc**E**pt = **E**mbrace it; **EX**cept = **EX**clude it. ad**A**pt = **A**lter; ad**O**pt = **O**wn it.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) is for actions in progress now or over a current period and for trends; state verbs stay simple. Accept (verb) vs except (not including); adapt (change to suit) vs adopt (take as your own).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Can I ____ your umbrella? I'll return it tomorrow."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The speaker wants to take and later return the umbrella.

**Step 2:** "borrow" = take for a time.

**Step 3:** "lend" would mean the speaker gives it.

**Tip:** Present continuous can describe a temporary situation around now (this week, these days). Watch confusing pairs: lie/lay, rise/raise, borrow/lend, wear/dress.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The temperature goes up by itself, with no object.

**Step 2:** Use "rise", which takes no object.

**Step 3:** Singular subject, general fact: rises.

**Tip:** Present continuous can describe a temporary situation around now (this week, these days). Watch confusing pairs: lie/lay, rise/raise, borrow/lend, wear/dress.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Don't ____ on the wet grass; you'll catch a cold."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The meaning is to rest your body flat, with no object.

**Step 2:** Use "lie".

**Step 3:** "lay" needs an object (lay the book).

**Tip:** Present continuous can describe a temporary situation around now (this week, these days). Watch confusing pairs: lie/lay, rise/raise, borrow/lend, wear/dress.

glossary.meaning: A verb for a state, not an action (know, like, belong): not used in -ing form.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.label: 18. Which sentence is correct?

similar.q: Complete: That colour really ____ you.
Complete: Your shoes ____ your bag.

options.A: The dress doesn't fit me; it's too small.
options.B: The dress isn't fitting with me; it's too small.
options.C: The dress doesn't suit me; it's too small.
options.D: The dress doesn't match me; it's too small.

why: Answer A: The dress doesn't fit me; it's too small.
"fit" refers to size; "suit" refers to how good something looks on you; "match" means go well with another thing.
"too small" is about size, so "fit" is correct.
The last option uses the wrong form.

why: True. The present continuous with "this year" suggests a limited period.
